findings: research-funding-discovery-platform / commercial:clarivate-pivot-rp: the snapshot saved for https://exlibrisgroup.com/products/pivot-funding-opportunities-and-profiles/ (sha256 b36d0104545ecc6086265ac89f236b993d304f29248805db7c281cfa9556e749) is the Ex Libris corporate homepage and contains no mention of Pivot, Pivot-RP, funding opportunities, or discovery; the official source therefore does not substantiate the product or its type. The entry must be supported by a correct product-page snapshot or removed/narrowed; the current case_found assertion is unsupported.
non_blocking_notes: Agilent iLab snapshot demonstrates core listing and service requests but not pricing/recharge; acceptable for a commercial basic record, but the leaf reason should not overstate charging evidence.

OpenGov snapshot is homepage navigation showing Permitting & Licensing and Building & Inspections modules; sufficient for basic commercial type matching, but it documents module presence rather than detailed workflows.

DSpace is reused for both digital-library-platform and institutional-repository; the type boundary is contested, but the correspondence is documented and should be retained rather than treated as a duplicate-product rejection.
Kuali Research is reused for both research-administration-platform and research-grant-management; this matches the documented alias relationship between those types.

The four insufficient_evidence leaves (research-compliance-management, research-lims, scientific-instrument-management, election-management-system) are valid documented gaps and do not require case_found.
Several open-source reasons are generic; wording can be tightened, but this does not affect authenticity or type matching.
